sn12.51:3.1: Pali is rich in expressions for inner reflection and investigation. Sometimes this process is called “inner self-examination” ([sn12.66:3.3](), sometimes “rational application of mind” ([sn12.4:2.3]()).
sn12.51:9.1: This is one of the passages showing that the primary sense of _saṅkhāra_ is moral “choices” either good, bad, or “imperturbable”. See also [mn57:9.2](), [an3.23](), [an4.233](). | The suffix _-upaga_ indicates “passing on” to rebirth in a new life. The compound _puññūpaga_ parallels _kammupaga_ and means “passes on by means of goodness” (resolve to _puññena upagataṁ_).
sn12.51:9.3: The fourth absorption and above are called “imperturbable” (_āneñja_) because they are associated with equanimous feeling. This is technically distinguished from “good” or “meritorious” (_puñña_) choices, whose outcome is pleasant feeling.
sn12.51:9.4: This shows that the sense of “choices” here is morally pregnant: they make no choice productive of future lives. They still make “choices” which are in line with the good, they just don’t have any kammic effect.
sn12.51:9.6: Letting go is not just a conceptual matter, it has immediate emotional consequences. _Paritassati_ conveys the twin senses of desire and agitation, for which “anxiety” seems the best fit.
sn12.51:10.1: This describes the reflective experience of the arahant.
sn12.51:11.2: To “become cool” is, as the simile makes clear, to realize extinguishment (_nibbāna_).
